about: The closed inventory of the priced sources' hex placeholders (base/hex_inventory.py; README section 'Hex placeholders: the closed inventory'). Every {:x}-family placeholder the run's template inventory holds, at any multiplicity, has exactly one entry here, keyed by its site (file:line, the line its format macro starts on), its argument key (G6's audit_key) and its format spec; text_budget.py stops the run on a placeholder with no entry, an entry with no placeholder, or a pin that does not match. The keys are written at `revision` and carried to the priced revision by the rule tables' own line map (lib/linemap_rules.py, without pruning); a carried key whose pins all match is a re-key, recorded in summary.json, not a re-audit. Threat model: the priced sources are our own code under ordinary maintenance (comments, aliases, shadowing and innocently named variables are inside the model, and so is a test constructed to expose a defect); source arranged to match a pin while changing its meaning is outside it. Use items are pinned only where an entry's reason names them (form "use"), not as a whole file. Each size is a reviewed bound on the premises its entry names; the proof is the audit recorded in the entry (its reason and premises), and the pins only detect a change to what was audited. Line numbers in a reason are at `revision`.
